idiom_name: module of async functions over a pg/mysql2 Pool (rows as plain objects)
implementation_notes: Node has no SQL in its standard library, so the gateway is built on the dominant driver: pg or mysql2 expose a connection Pool whose query(text, values) binds values by placeholder and returns rows already keyed by column name - the records are plain objects, exactly the shape the pattern wants. The classic object collapses into a module (or a small class holding the pool) with one async function per statement per table; query builders such as knex give the same boundary as a per-table builder, db('users').where({id}).first(), for those who prefer composable expressions over SQL strings. Keep the pool at process scope and pass it in; do not let the gateway own transactions, which are scoped by the caller's client checkout.
pitfalls: Checking out a client manually without client.release() in a finally block leaks a pool slot per request until the pool is exhausted.
PostgreSQL numeric/bigint columns arrive as strings in pg unless type parsers are configured, so a nominal record shape can carry unexpected runtime types.
Template literals in SQL text are injection as soon as a caller value is interpolated; the driver's parameter array exists precisely to avoid it.
Awaiting inside a for-loop over a pooled client serialises round trips; batch with a single statement or a transaction when the writes belong together.
